rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes adding ~5 at.% Ti to NbMoTaW, while the target study adds 20 at.% Re to form an equiatomic NbMoTaWRe film. Both are compositional modifications of the same base alloy, but the specific element and amount differ.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis mentions room-temperature, 1600 °C, and irradiation testing, but the target study only performs room-temperature He-ion irradiation and nanoindentation/compression on as-deposited films. The 1600 °C condition is absent in the target.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes grain-boundary segregation of Ti to enhance cohesion and ductility. The target mechanism involves Re-induced grain refinement, lattice distortion, excess free volume, and amorphous grain-boundary regions acting as defect sinks to suppress He-bubble growth and embrittlement. These are different mechanistic pathways.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts improved room-temperature ductility without compromising high-temperature strength or irradiation resistance. The target study reports improved He-irradiation resistance (less hardening, less embrittlement) at room temperature, but does not address high-temperature performance or baseline ductility improvement in the same way.
